## Elderly Care startups: the landscape

Elderly care companies serve ageing populations — home care platforms and staffing, remote monitoring and fall detection, medication management, care coordination between families and providers, and the software running residential and long-term care facilities. Payment usually comes from insurers or government programmes rather than the person receiving care.

Seedtable tracks 19 funded elderly care startups, ranked by the Seedtable Score from real funding, stage and traction data. The 19 top-ranked elderly care companies have raised $291M between them. Most sit at Series A and Series B stage. The leading hubs are United States, Berlin and Petah Tikva. Patronus, Biobeat and Age Care Labs lead the 2026 ranking, in a field mostly founded since 2014. Each entry links to the full profile — funding history, founders and investors — so you can see which elderly care companies are raising and growing right now.

## Why elderly care matters

The demographics are unambiguous and the care workforce is not growing to match, so anything that lets one carer cover more people or keeps someone at home longer has a clear buyer. Reimbursement for home-based and remote care has expanded, which is what made these businesses fundable rather than merely necessary.
